1: ✦In the first week, the baby hasn't actually implanted in your womb yet.✦Pregnancy lasts 40 weeks, but it is counted from the first day of your last period, not from implantation.✦During the first week, an egg cell starts to develop in your left or right ovary.
2: ✦Before your baby starts growing, you set the stage.✦Last week's rise in estrogen and progestin in your blood prompted your womb to build a rich, blood-filled lining ready for a possible fertilized egg.✦At the same time, eggs are maturing in fluid-filled sacs in your ovaries called follicles.
3: ✦At the start of this week (usually around day 14 of a 28-day cycle) you ovulated.✦One of your eggs left its follicle and travelled to the fallopian tube.✦Over the next 12–24 hours, one of the roughly 250 million sperm released by your partner will swim through the vagina, pass the cervix, enter the womb and try to reach and enter the egg in the fallopian tube.✦If it succeeds, the egg will be fertilized.✦About 400 sperm survive this journey, and only one manages to break through the egg's membrane.
4: ✦Over the next 30 hours, the nuclei of the sperm and the egg will join to combine their genetic material.✦If the sperm carries a Y chromosome, your baby will be a boy; if it carries an X chromosome, you'll have a girl.
5: ✦On its 3–4 day journey from the fallopian tube to the womb, the fertilized egg – the zygote – divides into 16 identical cells.✦Once it reaches the womb, the zygote is called a morula.✦One or two days later it settles into the lining of your womb and continues its amazing development and transformation.
6: ✦At this stage your developing baby is just a tiny ball of cells, scientifically called a blastocyst.✦The blastocyst has an inner cell mass that will form the embryo and an outer cell mass that will form the placenta; there is also a fluid-filled cavity that will become the amniotic sac.✦The outer cell mass becomes the placenta, the organ that brings oxygen and nutrients to your baby and carries waste away.
7: ✦Your last period started 12 to 16 days ago.✦So you're probably ovulating now or will ovulate soon.✦Although pregnancy really lasts about 38 weeks, the exact moment egg and sperm meet can't be known, so doctors calculate the due date as 40 weeks from the start of your last period.✦That's why you're already counted as 2 weeks pregnant when fertilization happens.✦Timing really matters if you want to conceive.✦To improve your chances, have intercourse between 72 hours before and 24 hours after ovulation.✦This lines up the sperm's 72-hour lifespan with the egg's 24-hour lifespan.✦Your partner should keep this window free too.✦To ease the pressure on both of you, it helps to know how long conception usually takes.✦Most couples only announce a pregnancy after several tries.✦If you're trying to conceive and still drink, smoke or take medicines, now is the time to stop.✦Your body should be in the best possible shape for the baby.✦Talk to your doctor about starting folic acid and vitamin supplements to lower the risk of birth defects.
8: ✦In the second week of pregnancy (around day 14 of a 28-day cycle) the released egg is pushed into the fallopian tube.✦Within the next 12 to 24 hours, out of about 250 million sperm making the tough 10-hour journey through the vagina, cervix and uterus to the fallopian tube, around 400 survive and only one enters the egg's membrane.✦The surge in LH peaks within 24 to 36 hours; this process, commonly known as ovulation, ends with the mature egg being fertilized by the right sperm.
9: ✦When the due date is calculated, counting starts before fertilization – from week 2 – even though sperm and egg haven't met yet.✦Women have about a 25% chance of getting pregnant in each menstrual cycle.
10: ✦After its 3–4 day journey from the fallopian tube to the uterus, the fertilized egg is now called a zygote and divides into 16 identical cells.✦When the zygote enters the uterus it's called a morula.✦Growing at an astonishing pace over 1–2 days, the morula burrows into the uterine wall and settles there.
11: ✦By now your developing baby has become a small ball of cells, called a blastocyst at this stage.✦This cluster of cells is the embryo itself.✦The sac filled with amniotic fluid is connected to the placenta.✦The placenta is the organ that carries the oxygen and nutrients your baby needs to live.
12: ✦Changes continue in both the baby and the mother-to-be in the first weeks of pregnancy.✦The baby keeps growing during these weeks.✦The endometrium – the lining of the womb – starts to thicken.✦This thickening allows the embryo formed after fertilization to attach securely to the womb.✦Blood flow to this area increases to meet the needs of your newly developing baby.
13: ✦Once the embryo settles in your womb, the little ball of cells splits in two.✦One part will form the embryo and the other the placenta.✦The placenta is an organ that forms during pregnancy, feeds your baby around the clock and leaves the womb together with the baby once its job is done.✦Your metabolism, changing with pregnancy hormones, and your womb are already working together to build the system that will carry oxygen and nutrients to the new embryo and placenta.
14: ✦Sperm, scientifically called spermatozoa, are the male reproductive cells.✦Sperm production in the testes begins at puberty.✦Each sperm cell has 3 parts.✦These are the head, the midpiece and the tail.✦A healthy man releases 150–200 million sperm during intercourse.✦But only about 1,000 sperm manage to get close to the egg.✦Of these, the fastest and most active sperm succeeds in fertilizing the egg.✦The egg must also be ready for fertilization to happen.
15: ✦A lot is happening in your belly right now.✦Your baby is a ball of cells growing at a furious pace.✦This ball of cells is called a blastocyst.
16: ✦Once the blastocyst implants in the womb, the part that will form the placenta begins producing the pregnancy hormone hCG.✦This hormone tells your ovaries to stop releasing eggs.✦It also triggers high production of estrogen and progesterone.
17: ✦The hCG hormone is what makes a pregnancy test turn positive.✦A pregnancy test taken at the end of this week will be positive.✦(If the test is negative and your period hasn't come, try again in a few days.)
18: ✦In the cavity that will become the amniotic sac, amniotic fluid starts collecting around the blastocyst.✦This fluid will cushion and protect your baby in the coming weeks and months.
19: ✦Right now your tiny blastocyst gets oxygen and nutrients and removes waste through a simple circulation of microscopic channels connected to the small blood vessels in your womb.✦Next week the placenta will take over this job.
20: ✦A few days after the important meeting of sperm and egg in your body, the fertilized egg is no longer just one cell.✦Your baby is still very small, but the number of cells grows by the hour.✦This cluster of cells, also called the zygote, travels down the fallopian tube toward the womb this week.✦The journey takes about 6 days; when the zygote reaches the womb, it takes up the position where it will grow for 9 months.✦As the cells keep multiplying, some become the embryo and some form the placenta.✦Then production of hCG, known as the pregnancy hormone, begins.✦Thanks to this hormone your body stops producing eggs and increases estrogen and progesterone.✦Meanwhile, amniotic fluid fills the space around the zygote, forming the amniotic sac that will cushion it for months.✦Until the placenta develops enough to do its job, your baby gets oxygen and nutrients – and removes waste – through a simple circulation of microscopic channels connected to the vessels in the uterine wall.
21: ✦Although you won't know for a while, your 3-week-old baby's sex is already decided.✦Your fertilized egg has 46 chromosomes – 23 from the mother and 23 from the father. Of the two types, X and Y, the X chromosome always comes from the mother.✦The chromosome from the father can be either X or Y.✦If the baby has XX chromosomes, you'll hold a girl in your arms in 9 months; if XY, a boy.
22: ✦This week of pregnancy signals the start of the embryonic period.✦From now until week 10, all of your baby's organs – and even some of their functions – begin to develop.✦This makes it the period when your baby's development is most vulnerable to any disruption.✦Right now the baby is an embryo about the size of a poppy seed.✦This poppy-seed-sized embryo (about 3 mm) contains layers called the epiblast and hypoblast.
23: ✦While you're still wondering whether you're pregnant, your baby has already found its place.✦The blastocyst has completed its journey from the fallopian tube to the womb.✦The burrows it makes in the lining of the womb create connections that will last through the last 8 months of pregnancy (and, in a way, a lifetime).✦Very soon the tiny cells settled in the womb divide into two groups.✦One group will become the embryo itself, while the other shapes the channels the baby will use to receive nutrients and remove waste throughout life in the womb.
24: ✦Although the embryo is smaller than 1 mm, its development is very intense.✦As the amniotic sac forms around the embryo, the yolk sac is also forming.✦The yolk sac will later help start up the baby's developing digestive system.✦The embryo now has three distinct layers of cells, each growing into specific parts of the baby's body.✦The innermost layer, the endoderm, gives rise to the digestive system, liver and lungs.✦The middle layer, the mesoderm, forms the heart, sex organs, bones, kidneys and muscles.✦The outermost layer, the ectoderm, forms the nervous system, hair, skin and eyes.
25: ✦This week marks the beginning of the embryonic period.✦From today until your tenth week, all your baby's organs will start to develop, and some will even start working.
26: ✦Your embryo is the size of a poppy seed and at its most sensitive to anything that could threaten its development.
27: ✦Your placenta is forming; by the end of this week it will start passing nutrients from your blood to your baby.
28: ✦Meanwhile, the amniotic sac your baby is growing in is producing red blood cells.✦This way it nourishes your baby until the placenta takes over.
29: ✦Your baby is now about the size of a sesame seed.✦Your baby keeps growing fast.
30: ✦At this stage the embryo is made of layers called the ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.✦The ectoderm is the layer where the brain, spinal cord, nerves and spine develop.✦The ectoderm also forms the skin, hair, nails, tooth enamel, and milk and sweat glands.
31: ✦The second layer, the mesoderm, is where the heart and circulatory system form.✦It also forms muscles, cartilage, bones and the tissue under the skin.
32: ✦The endoderm layer shapes the lungs, intestines, urinary system, thyroid, kidneys and pancreas.✦From this week, the placenta and umbilical cord start doing their job.
33: ✦This week, in the inner layer called the endoderm, cells that will form the endocrine glands, digestive system and bladder begin to take shape.✦As the circulatory system begins to form, the baby's tiny heart starts beating, though you can't hear it yet.✦You'll be able to hear your baby's heartbeat at an ultrasound around weeks 10 to 12.
34: ✦Can the baby be seen this week? A 5-week gestational sac can only be seen with a transvaginal ultrasound.✦But it's normal not to see the baby or the heartbeat inside the sac yet.✦That's simply because the baby is still too small to be seen.
35: ✦Sex in the fifth week of pregnancy is completely harmless.✦In a normal pregnancy there are no restrictions on your sex life until the last 4 weeks.✦But you may not always feel like it.✦In the first trimester, including this week, hormonal swings, nausea and tiredness can dull your desire.✦This usually changes in the second trimester.
36: ✦This week your baby's mouth, ears and nose have started to take shape.
37: ✦If you could look inside your womb, you'd see a head with small dark spots on it.✦Those are your baby's eyes and nostrils.✦The two little hollows on the sides of the head are the ears.
38: ✦The arms and legs have started to form.✦The heart beats 100–160 times a minute.✦Blood has started to flow around the body.
39: ✦The intestines are developing, and the bud that will later become the lungs has appeared.✦The pituitary gland and the rest of the brain, the bones and muscles are taking shape.
40: ✦This week your baby is the size of a lentil, but by the end of the week will be three times bigger.✦The nose, mouth and ears you won't be able to stop looking at in 8 months start to form this week.✦If you could look inside your womb, you'd see the head with dark spots where the eyes are forming.✦The developing ears are already making small bumps on the sides of the head.
